A conference deck spends most of its life on a projector in a bright room, where a busy theme is a liability.

`coeos` is dark and restrained: a full title slide, a logo in the corner, a footer carrying the author and licence, and slide numbers, with nothing else competing for attention.

[See a deck built by this site](preview.html).

![](preview.html){.embed-art loading="lazy" title="A deck in the coeos theme" style="--atelier-embed-art-ratio: 1.78;"}

## Starting a presentation

```bash
quarto use template {{< var extension.reference >}}
```

::: {.btn-group role="group" aria-label="Quarto Wizard installer options"}

[Visual Studio Code](vscode://mcanouil.quarto-wizard/use?repo={{< var extension.wizard-reference >}}){.btn .btn-outline-primary title="Use {{< var extension.reference >}} in Visual Studio Code using the Quarto Wizard extension."}

## Adding it to a presentation you already have

```bash
quarto add {{< var extension.reference >}}
```

This will install the extension under the `_extensions` subdirectory.
If you are using version control, you will want to check in this directory.

::: {.btn-group role="group" aria-label="Quarto Wizard installer options"}

## Quick start

```yaml
format: coeos-revealjs
```

The theme takes the title, subtitle, author, institute, and date from the front matter and lays out the title slide from them.

See the [Reference](reference.qmd) for what it styles, and the [Examples](examples.qmd) for the source behind the deck.

## Where it works

RevealJS.
